checks.name: 100 vs 100 battle comparison
checks.scope: One controlled 30-second native A/B: mean frame 71.1→65.3 ms; p95 127.7→116.7 ms. Worst frame 175.4→217.8 ms; occasional spikes and input latency tails remain. Synthetic reinforcements maintain 100 living units each.

checks.name: Protocol compatibility
checks.scope: Immutable final source: current protocol 7 joins and starts; old protocol 6 rejected clearly. Sources unchanged and owned processes exited.

checks.name: Reproducible release
checks.scope: Independent reproduction, hash closure, cache/update tests and isolated Linux-server smoke. No unrelated services restarted.

limitations: No physical phone, tablet or Safari/PWA speaker test. The previous module-import errors support the startup fix, but the precise WebKit failure and the user’s silent session are not proven resolved on their device.

The 100-per-player benchmark is a synthetic native workload and one comparison pair, not a sustained 60 FPS claim. Average and p95 frame times improved, but the maximum frame and input-latency tails did not.
Solo requires one completed download and browser storage retention. Online requires a connection. A changed game pack downloads as one whole file; unchanged files are reused.
Undo is a ten-second, one-level recovery for eligible explicit group worker orders. It does not rewind resources, damage, position or completed work; unavailable old jobs stop safely.
The deployment checks for connections immediately before replacement but does not atomically close new admissions. Both observed guards were empty.

native_battle_comparison.scope: One quiet sequential native Windows run per whole runtime, approximately 30 seconds per sample; identical fixture, assets, settings and import cache. Synthetic reinforcements maintain 100 living units per player.
native_battle_comparison.conclusion: Current whole runtime improved mean and p95 frame time in this matched pair; p99 effectively unchanged; single maximum frame worse. Earlier broad recorded regression did not reproduce in this pair. This does not establish smooth frame pacing or physical-device performance.
